graphEvents.label: Does post-pin public work change the packet?
An architecture write is a page-level node set, not one node
ERD connector caps are missing from the corpus parser

label: Figma's own project-plan block names the discovery rule the packet lacks for created nodes: capture the diagram node id the tool returns, or fall back to scanning page children when it returns nothing.

An architecture diagram written with FIGMA_DIAGRAM_2026 is a page-level set of one to two SECTION nodes plus multiple SHAPE_WITH_TEXT and CONNECTOR nodes, so the packet's one-write-one-diagram assumption and its stop-on-unrecognised-node rollback both need the set rule.

Figma's documented ConnectorStrokeCap union includes ARROW_EQUILATERAL, ARROW_LINES, TRIANGLE_FILLED, DIAMOND_FILLED, CIRCLE_FILLED and five ERD caps, while the corpus parser counts only an ARROW_ prefix, TRIANGLE_FILLED or the undocumented LINE_ARROW, so an ERD crows-foot would read as undirected.

Read tools are rationed by plan, with a Starter plan or a View or Collab seat limited to six tool calls a month while write tools are exempt, and the packet's read-back plus screenshot plus tag chain never mentions the allowance in its gate.

Figma's own pinned tree still carries two incompatible generate_diagram call shapes, mermaidSyntax with an optional fileKey in the skill and mermaid plus editorType figjam in the workflow block, so the run-time confirmation rule is the only safe position and the packet should say the disagreement exists.

Figma states that every generate_diagram call without a fileKey creates a new draft file and that regenerating four times leaves four drafts, a user-visible cost the packet's fileKey rule never gives a reason for.

Post-pin public material adds distribution rather than discipline: a Slides variant of the use_figma skill, a Figma community skills page and a blog post announcing the FigJam skills and architecture layouts, none of which contradicts a protected behaviour or adds a check.

The architecture layout code is documented as the value of the useArchitectureLayoutCode parameter on generate_diagram, and the packet already passes FIGMA_DIAGRAM_2026 for architecture only, so this is a confirmation rather than a gap.
